expected.summary: Eleven minutes before the anchor the platform team changed a route table (NET-882, NAT capacity for us-east-1c) so that nodes ip-10-0-9-14 and ip-10-0-9-37 send internet traffic through a new NAT gateway, nat-0b7e21, with public address 3.91.204.17; the pods on those nodes logged the change, among them shipping-3 and shipping-6. shipping books every checkout with the carrier api.shipco.example.com, which only accepts calls from allowlisted source addresses, and 3.91.204.17 is not on the list. From that moment every booking from shipping-3 and shipping-6 is refused: shipping answers 502 carrier api.shipco.example.com returned 403: source address 3.91.204.17 is not permitted for account SHOP-4471, while the four other shipping pods book normally. About a third of POST /checkout requests fail, after the card has been charged, and the failures propagate through checkout, web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires; no other route calls shipping. payment-3 and payment-6 moved to the same NAT and are healthy, since the payment provider does not filter by source address. shipping's version did not change and nothing shipped. The SEA-3 label format change (WH-219, PDF to ZPL) logged on shipping three minutes earlier is unrelated: it applies to one warehouse's labels and fails no booking.
contributingFactors: the NET-882 route table change sending two nodes out through nat-0b7e21
the carrier's source address allowlist not including 3.91.204.17
shipping booking inline after payment on every checkout

criteria.description: Does the brief name the NET-882 route table change sending shipping-3 and shipping-6 out through the new NAT gateway nat-0b7e21 as the trigger, with the carrier refusing the new source address because it is not allowlisted, and the failed bookings failing checkout through the BFFs to edge-gateway? 5 = the NAT change, the allowlist, the two pods only and the victim chain. Calling it a carrier outage or blaming the label format change scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in the 403 not permitted errors on shipping spans naming 3.91.204.17, the failures confined to shipping-3 and shipping-6, the network.event lines on those pods at onset, and payment-3 and payment-6 staying healthy on the same NAT? Cap at 3 unless it explains why only two shipping pods fail.
Does it avoid blaming the WH-219 label format change, a carrier outage, payment or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
